Long ago, Baleetles scoured the land for quality stone balls to bring back to Berylline Vale. One Baleetle found a perfect stone, but failed to push it over the mountain and bring it back. Every time it neared the peak, the ball rolled back down, dragging the Baleetle with it. Over time, this created a strange, straight path up the mountain. One day, the earth shook, the mountain crumbled, and a stone wall marked with the words "mountain path" fell onto Berylline Vale, which was the only proof of this event. Later, other Baleetles saw this "mountain path" and used it as a natural racetrack. Years later, the rock turned pure cyan, nurturing a stoneflower within—a symbol of life blooming in the wrong place.
Do we still need to go deeper?
